step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture processes acoustic data from IoT devices to detect water leaks. First, IoT devices (e.g., smart fire hydrants) send daily acoustic signals to an API Gateway for secure ingestion. The API Gateway then persists these files in an S3 bucket. A daily batch process running on ECS consumes these files from S3 to perform processor-intensive acoustic correlation algorithms. The persistent correlations found by ECS are then fed to an AWS SageMaker ML endpoint, which classifies them and assigns a leak probability score. Finally, these leak scores are provided to human analysts who further qualify the leaks and may initiate field investigations. A feedback loop exists where analysts' input is used to retrain the SageMaker model every six weeks to improve accuracy.

nodes.name: IoT Device
nodes.notes: Smart fire hydrants, meters, and other IoT devices collecting acoustic, pressure, and water quality data from the pipe network.

nodes.name: API Gateway
nodes.notes: Receives daily acoustic signals from IoT devices, providing authentication and security before passing data to S3.

nodes.name: Data Lake S3
nodes.notes: Bucket for persisting raw acoustic signal files received via API Gateway.

nodes.name: Batch Processing ECS
nodes.notes: Containerized service running daily batch processes with processor-intensive acoustic algorithms to find correlations in the S3 data.

nodes.name: ML Endpoint SageMaker
nodes.notes: Machine learning endpoint that classifies persistent correlations received from ECS, assigning a probability (leak score).

nodes.name: Human Analyst
nodes.notes: Company analysts who receive leak scores from SageMaker, further qualify potential leaks, and provide feedback for model retraining.
